title: Preserve shared public collections during account deletion
classification: Confirmed policy mismatch: user-owned public collections were deleted by the owner foreign-key CASCADE even though other members could read them.

change.behavior: Account deletion deletes private non-system collections and cascaded items; public or system collections and their items remain with owner_user_id cleared.
change.schema: The owner FK now uses ON DELETE SET NULL. Alembic revision e1f2a3b4c5d6 upgrades existing schemas; no collection row is migrated or removed by the schema migration.
change.manifest: R1994 replaces the earlier R1989 disposition for game_collections.owner_user_id with a conditional public-retain/private-delete policy.

verification.result: passed: 19 tests in 112.51 seconds on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6 against a fresh disposable schema migrated through e1f2a3b4c5d6; the child-role departing account fixture ran and the database was dropped after the run.
verification.assertions: The populated relation fixture seeds a public collection/item and a private collection/item for the departing child account; it asserts the public row/item survive ownerless and the private row/item are deleted.
verification.schema: Current ORM and Alembic head e1f2a3b4c5d6.

limits: The behavior is verified against the current disposable PostgreSQL schema, not a deployed operator schema.
Existing private collection content is deleted after migration because account deletion classifies it as private user data.
